neighbours.label: a verb of flat denial or refutation in argumentative prose ('the data refute the model', 'flatly contradicts'), as against neutral or supportive verbs in the same frame
fire: Critics argue that the new measurements flatly refute the standard model of the ocean currents.
In her reply, the historian shows that the letters directly contradict the official account of the trial.
Several later studies have decisively disproved the claim that the vaccine causes the disorder.
The defence lawyer set out to rebut every point the prosecution had raised about the alibi.
His own diary entries plainly contradict what he later told the committee under oath.
Geologists say the rock layers firmly refute the idea that the canyon formed in a single flood.
The second experiment conclusively disproved the theory that the metal loses mass when heated.
In the article, the author tries to refute the popular belief that bats are blind.
quiet: Critics argue that the new measurements broadly support the standard model of the ocean currents.
In her reply, the historian shows that the letters closely follow the official account of the trial.
Several later studies have carefully examined the claim that the vaccine causes the disorder.
The defence lawyer set out to summarise every point the prosecution had raised about the alibi.
His own diary entries largely match what he later told the committee under oath.
Geologists say the rock layers clearly record the idea that the canyon formed over millions of years.
The second experiment carefully measured how the metal changes colour when heated.
In the article, the author tries to explain the popular belief that bats are blind.
